english: Why did the god take my son, old man? The gods take the one whom they love. What did I do? You did nothing. The god did not ask; he snatches. Will he give him back? He will not give him back. Give the god a cow, so that he may not seize your daughter. I give him my best cow.
uncertain: mē h1pyéh1t read as optative of h1ep 'seize'

english: Why did the oak burn again? Perkwunos struck it with his thunder. Did he strike our house too? He did not strike our house; he struck the house of that man who deceived the gods. Did the people in that house perish? All perished in the fire. Have you feared Perkwunos? I fear him, and I do not deceive the gods.
uncertain: kl1h2tóm is a participle with no finite verb: 'it [is] struck'
pérkwunos taken as genitive or nominative unclear
kélh2t read as aorist 'struck', from kelh2 'strike'

english: Perkwunos, hear us, god. We offer you a white ox together. Drink the blood, eat the fat. Take the ox; do not take our young men. Do not burn our house and our cows. Strike the oaks and the stones.

The water-spirit (nébhtus?) dwells beneath the ford. In one summer it took a man. It drags him down by the feet. No one saw him. The young man did not fear the god. At night he went into the ford(?) with his two horses. One horse alone ran back home in the morning. The spirit took the young man and did not let him go. His mother searched for him every year at the bank.

The king left the corpse for the dogs in the field. No one covered him; all feared the king. Then his sister spoke in the darkness. She threw earth on him with her hands. She poured water and milk and dug [a grave] for him. The dogs did not eat him. The king saw that in the morning and raged.
uncertain: h3rēǵsú is locative plural, but fear should take the ablative of a single king

english: Mother-in-law, I saw my husband in a dream. What did he say to you? He said nothing. He stood at the door and wailed and trembled. The dead hunger because no one feeds them. Pour milk and mead on his stone this evening. Will he come back? He will not come back, because he will be filled. I will pour it this evening.
